\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شرط} (sharṭ)}{شرط (sharṭ)}]{\ar{شرط} (sharṭ) — a condition}

\label{lesson:AR-C404-shart}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for most probably, then the Arabic for in general.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شرط}}
\textbf{\ar{شرط}} — \emph{sharṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a condition\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لي} \ar{شرط} \ar{واحد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lī sharṭ wāḥid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have one condition.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{شروط}, \emph{shurūṭ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شرط}} (\emph{sharṭ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-r-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to set a mark; to stipulate\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{sharṭ} is a mark set down in a bargain: a condition. \ar{شرطة}, the police, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lī sharṭ wāḥid.} — I have one condition.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for most probably, then the Arabic for in general, then say \emph{sharṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شرط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A condition\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اشترط} (ishtaraṭa)}{اشترط (ishtaraṭa)}]{\ar{اشترط} (ishtaraṭa) — to stipulate}

\label{lesson:AR-C404-ishtarata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for in general, then the Arabic for a condition.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اشترط}}
\textbf{\ar{اشترط}} — \emph{ishtaraṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}to stipulate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اشترطت} \ar{الشركة} \ar{خبرة} \ar{سنتين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ishtaraṭat ash-sharika khibrat sanatayn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company stipulated two years of experience.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشترط}, \emph{yashtariṭ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اشترط}} (\emph{ishtaraṭa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-r-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to set a mark; to stipulate\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to set a condition for oneself: to stipulate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حتى} \ar{لو} (ḥattā law)}{حتى لو (ḥattā law)}]{\ar{حتى} \ar{لو} (ḥattā law) — even if}

\label{lesson:AR-C404-hatta-law}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a condition, then the Arabic for to stipulate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حتى} \ar{لو}}
\textbf{\ar{حتى} \ar{لو}} — \emph{ḥattā law} — \textquotedblleft{}even if\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سأذهب} \ar{حتى} \ar{لو} \ar{أمطرت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sa-adhhabu ḥattā law amṭarat.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I will go even if it rains.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حتى} \ar{لو}} (\emph{ḥattā law}) joins the native Arabic particles \emph{ḥattā}, \textquotedblleft{}even, until\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{law}, \textquotedblleft{}if\textquotedblright{}: even if. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كما} \ar{لو} (kamā law)}{كما لو (kamā law)}]{\ar{كما} \ar{لو} (kamā law) — as if}

\label{lesson:AR-C404-kama-law}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to stipulate, then the Arabic for even if.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كما} \ar{لو}}
\textbf{\ar{كما} \ar{لو}} — \emph{kamā law} — \textquotedblleft{}as if\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلم} \ar{كما} \ar{لو} \ar{كان} \ar{المدير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallama kamā law kāna al-mudīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كما} \ar{لو}} (\emph{kamā law}) joins the native Arabic \emph{kamā}, \textquotedblleft{}as\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{law}, \textquotedblleft{}if\textquotedblright{}: as if. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضمن} (ḍamina)}{ضمن (ḍamina)}]{\ar{ضمن} (ḍamina) — to ensure; to guarantee}

\label{lesson:AR-C404-damina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for even if, then the Arabic for as if.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضمن}}
\textbf{\ar{ضمن}} — \emph{ḍamina} — \textquotedblleft{}to ensure; to guarantee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ضمن} \ar{الأب} \ar{مستقبل} \ar{ابنه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍamina al-ab mustaqbal ibnih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The father secured his son's future.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يضمن}, \emph{yaḍman}.

Followed by \ar{أن}: \ar{ضمن} \ar{أن} …, made sure that ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضمن}} (\emph{ḍamina}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be surety for\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ḍamina} is a Form I verb, to stand surety: to guarantee, to ensure.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
